policy: verbatim copies of the import closure of the official world model (models.WorldModel with networks.RSSM / MultiEncoder / MultiDecoder / MLP / GRUCell / ConvEncoder / ConvDecoder and tools.Optimizer / OneHotDist / DiscDist / SymlogDist / symlog / static_scan / weight inits) plus the official configs.yaml (defaults read by the adapter) and LICENSE. Allowed edits: package-relative imports, and the one listed P-route compatibility edit in tools.py. Not vendored: dreamer.py, exploration.py, parallel.py, envs/ (online agent loop, actor-critic driver, environments). Decision P-license: https://github.com/Sino-Huang/NovPhy/issues/133#issuecomment-6388618813
runtime_notes: networks.MLP's default device='cuda' (MultiEncoder / MultiDecoder build their MLPs without a device) only feeds a fixed-std tensor that the encoder output path and the symlog_mse decoder path never read; on a CUDA-less host constructing it raises. The adapter (novphy.mlp_default_device) and the G-port reference set that default to the run device while a model is constructed; no file is edited (P-route).

models.WorldModel.preprocess divides obs['image'] by 255 unconditionally (upstream environments always deliver an image). The adapter's subclass applies it only when an image is present (vector-only carriers); the G-port reference feeds the official code a dummy image key that no encoder / decoder key selects.
Upstream runs torch.compile(WorldModel) by default (config compile True); the adapter runs eagerly (same graph, fp32).

edits: imports made package-relative: 'import networks' -> 'from . import networks', 'import tools' -> 'from . import tools' (lines 5-6)
import made package-relative: 'import tools' -> 'from . import tools' (line 10)

P-route compatibility: the module-level 'from torch.utils.tensorboard import SummaryWriter' (line 17) moved into Logger.__init__, its only user, so the module imports without tensorboard (not installed in the novphy env; Logger is never constructed by the adapter). No other line changed.
